text.en: Look at a tiled floor. The same shapes meet at corners again and again. Why do they fit so neatly?

A tiling pattern covers a surface with shapes without gaps. In the book, a pattern is made using two different shapes, squares and triangles.
At the marked points, notice which shapes meet. Are the same set of shapes meeting at each point? Continue the pattern and colour it.
Create your own patterns using cut-outs of other shapes and check that there are no gaps or overlaps.
Shapes with equal sides such as squares and equilateral triangles fit together well. Check the angles at the meeting point.
Patterns repeat. Look at rangoli, floor tiles and borders of saris for examples.
(additional, not in the textbook) At a corner of a tiling, the angles of the meeting shapes add up to a full turn.
